title: SLO-linked pager quarantine and automated multi-region failover playflows
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to get noisy pages for transient, localized degradation events (single AZ or warmup spikes) despite SLO-based thresholds. This drives context loss and on-call fatigue, and increases MTTR because responders are paged before automated mitigations and circuit handoffs run.

Goal: Implement a SLO-linked 'pager quarantine' mechanism that temporarily suppresses low-confidence pages during controlled error-budget burn patterns, while automatically executing a region-aware failover playflow that exercises circuit-breaker and load-shedding policies. The system must be observable, reversible by on-call, and auditable for compliance.

Scope & features: 
- Map SLO-derived signals (error budget burn rate, latency percentiles, active circuit trips) to paging confidence scores.
- Pager quarantine window: configurable short suppression (30s-10m) for noisy signals, with automatic re-evaluation and forced page if degradation persists or passes a severity threshold.
- Region-aware circuit handoff: when regional SLOs breach, trigger automated measured failover to healthy region(s) with gradual traffic shift and automatic rollback thresholds.
- Integrate automatic runbook execution: pre-flight checks (synthetic probe validation, replica health, cache warmup) executed during quarantine to validate whether human escalation is needed.
- Manual/automated controls in Console: allow on-call to apply immediate quarantines, escalate, or force failover. Audit log for all actions.
- Telemetry: add new Grafana dashboards and composed SLO metrics showing suppression events, prevented pages, and post-quarantine outcomes.

Trade-offs & risk mitigation:
- Risk: Suppression could mask a real incident. Mitigations: require multi-signal agreement for suppression (error budget + probe pass/fail), tight maximum quarantine window, forced page if error budget burn rate exceeds high threshold, and synthetic probes run every 15s during quarantine.
- Risk: Automated failover could increase latency or cost. Mitigations: staged traffic migration, canary routing, and pre-flight capacity checks.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Signal schema and scoring (ENG): define scoring rules and new metric names (slo_quarantine_score, regional_cb_state).
2) Short-lived suppression controller (ENG): implement controller in alerting pipeline (Prometheus Alertmanager extension or internal alert router) with feature flag.
3) Runbook automation hooks (ENG/Platform): build pluggable action runners that execute probes and circuit-handshake API calls.
4) Failover playflow engine (ENG/Infra): orchestrate region handoff with gradual routing adjustments and rollback checks.
5) Console UX (Product): controls for on-call and audit log display.
6) Observability (SRE): dashboards, SLO regressions and postmortem templates.

Success criteria:
- 40-60% reduction in low-confidence pages within two weeks of rollout for targeted services.
- No customer-impacting incidents masked (verified by postmortem sampling).
- Automated region failover completes within SLO-defined RTO in 90% of simulated events.

Acceptance criteria / rollout:
- Feature gated behind runtime-1.20 flag per service and region.
- Canary rollout to non-critical services, then to paid tenants on Dedicated.
- Telemetry verified and alert rules updated.

Links & artifacts: see attachments for design doc, dashboards, and PRs.
